documents.title: Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid Key Agreement Mechanisms for TLS 1.3
Post-Quantum Cryptography Recommendations for TLS-based Applications

standardisation.notes: Two documents, two jobs, and they are conflated constantly. RFC 9954 fixes the hybrid construction; RFC 10024 names the groups and its Section 1 states it applies the RFC 9954 framework to ML-KEM.

evidence.excerpt: Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid Key Agreement Mechanisms for TLS 1.3
The default TLS supported groups list has been changed to include and prefer hybrid PQC KEM groups. Some practically unused groups were removed from the default list.
The new post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 key exchange mechanism is now supported and is enabled by default when Config.CurvePreferences is nil. GODEBUG setting tlsmlkem=0 reverts the default.

implementation.notes: Deliberately incomplete, and both entries are first-party. BoringSSL, NSS and the browsers are widely reported to ship X25519MLKEM768 and are omitted rather than asserted, because they were not checked for this row.

interoperability.notes: No pairwise result is recorded. This is the honest value and it is itself the finding: the groups are on by default in two stacks and this matrix carries no evidence of what has been tested against what. PQUIP has the same gap in a free-text column.

failure_mode.on_negotiation_failure: TLS 1.3 aborts rather than completing classically: the Finished MAC authenticates the full handshake transcript, so an on-path attacker who edits the offered groups causes a failure and not a silent downgrade. The residual exposure is endpoint behaviour, not the protocol.

known_exposures.detail: Application or legacy logic that answers a failed hybrid handshake with a fresh classical-only attempt. A conformant TLS 1.3 client does not retract its offered groups, so this is endpoint behaviour, and it hands an attacker a downgrade by making the first attempt fail.
Classical groups listed ahead of hybrid ones produce classical sessions with no attacker present.
Hybrid enabled in configuration and never confirmed as negotiated in production.
Larger PQC ClientHello messages fragmented or dropped by middleboxes, where the common operational resolution is to disable hybrid to restore service.

Go: the hybrid default applies only when Config.CurvePreferences is nil, so any application that pins curve preferences silently does not get it, and the GODEBUG setting tlsmlkem=0 reverts the default fleet-wide. Go's own release notes give the operational reason operators flip it: buggy TLS servers that mishandle large records, causing a handshake timeout. This is the exposure the implementation excerpt originally hid by truncating before the condition.

evidence.excerpt: The Finished message is the final message in the Authentication Block. It is essential for providing authentication of the handshake and of the computed keys.

failure_mode.notes: This axis is why one score will not do. The protocol is published and on by default in two stacks and a deployment can still be classical end to end. Written up in QS06, so this points at the entry rather than restating it.
